reader.title: Simon Hoe and the Palace Hotel fire
bases: A1 describes a mentally deranged man in a burning hotel room firing at the Black man who came to put out the fire and subdue him; it reports no racial motive, no mob and no injury, and frames the item as praise for Hoe's bravery.
Only A1, itself a reprint of a Commonwealth item, reports the incident; no other account was found in either press.

summary.text: Simon Hoe and the Palace Hotel fire was an incident, reported in early August 1880, in which a deranged man who had set fire to his room at the Palace Hotel fired two shots at Simon Hoe, a Black man who climbed up with a fire hose to subdue him.
Hoe was not reported hurt, and the only account found presents him as a hero rewarded by the hotel's proprietor.
According to Col. Stanton of the Palace Hotel, a man described as "crazy" set his room on fire.
Hoe, called "a colored man" in the report, seized the hose, went up a ladder and broke open the window, and the man fired two shots at him.
Hoe then "cooled him off with a dose of water," entered the room alone and seized him.
The report does not give the date of the fire, the name or race of the man, or the town where the hotel stood.
Stanton called the act "a rare instance of bravery" and gave Hoe a ten-dollar bill.
No report of an arrest or of any charge against the man appears in the coverage.
The Topeka Tribune of 5 August 1880 carried the story under the headline "Simon Hoe the Hero," crediting it to the Commonwealth.
The item was a correction: it said an earlier notice had wrongly given a fireman credit for first taking the hose to the room.
It appeared among local notices and directly above a Lawrence Standard report on a meeting of "colored voters of Lawrence," but the Hoe item itself does not mention Lawrence.
No other paper in either press was found to have reported the fire or the shots.

accounts.label: Hotel proprietor's account via the Commonwealth
accounts.gist: Col. Stanton told the paper that Hoe, not a fireman, first took the hose to the room, was shot at twice, cooled the man off with water and seized him alone.

framing.detail: A short local item headlined 'Simon Hoe the Hero' that credits Hoe's bravery and corrects an earlier report giving the credit to a fireman.

record_check.dossier: Accurate as to the act, but the item is a tribute to Hoe's bravery in fighting the fire and reports no racial motive or injury.

sources.note: Local item 'Simon Hoe the Hero', credited to the Commonwealth: per Col. Stanton of the Palace Hotel, Simon Hoe, a colored man, took the hose up a ladder to a crazy man's burning room, was fired at twice and seized the man; Stanton gave him $10.
quotes: He siezed the hose, went up the ladder, broke open the window, had two shots fired at him, cooled him off with a dose of water, and went into the room alone and seized the man.
The Colonel thinks it was a rare instance of bravery, and he was so well pleased about it that he presented Mr. Hoe with a ten dollar bill.
